items.title: Bound Tiberian Dawn's reinforcement retries at the map edge
items.details:
- `EnterFromEdge()` (`td/ai/reinforcements.cc:121`) retries a member from a neighbouring edge cell whenever `Unlimbo()` fails, with no limit. items.title: Fix the source sampling in ScaleRotateShape(), then step the coordinates incrementally
items.details:
`ra/assets/shape_draw.cc`.

The destination-to-source mapping has three defects, visible on an 8x6 test shape at a half turn, at west, and at north with scale 0x180:

- It maps each destination pixel's corner (`x - width`), not its centre, so the result sits one pixel off the centre of the doubled frame.
- `static_cast<int>` truncates toward zero, so source coordinates in (-1, 1) all become 0: the first source row and column are drawn one pixel too wide (13 columns where 12 are right at scale 1.5).
- At quarter turns `std::cos`/`std::sin` return about 1e-16 instead of 0, so coordinates that should be exact integers fall on either side of a pixel boundary and rows come out spliced or duplicated.

Fix: sample the pixel centre (`x + 0.5 - width`, `y + 0.5 - height`), take `floor`, and use exact matrix entries (0, +-1) when the angle is a multiple of 64. Expected results: a half turn of an 8x6 shape is the source reversed in columns 4..11, rows 3..8; north at scale 1.5 is 12x9 in columns 2..13, rows 1..9 with every source pixel 1 or 2 wide. Add golden unit tests for these (the function has none); it changes how every rotated or scaled shape draws, usually by a one-pixel shift, so re-record the `tools/ui_check.py` screenshots that change.

Then step the source coordinates per x (start computed once per row, a constant added per pixel) instead of four multiplies per pixel. Measured 2026-10-05 on the current mapping: 11.3 -> 8.0 us per 48x48 shape, but 5,503 of 10,240 rotation/scale/size cases moved pixels, 90% of them at quarter turns, because the accumulated rounding crosses the same exact boundaries. With centre sampling only 175 cases differ (odd-sized shapes at quarter turns, where a half-pixel centre still lands on a boundary); keep the stepping only if the golden tests and a sweep of all 256 rotations show it reproduces the corrected output exactly, e.g. by using the exact integer path for quarter turns. `std::floor` is a libm call without SSE4.1 and cost more than the stepping saved (30 vs 11 us), so floor with integer arithmetic or an offset that keeps the value positive.

items.title: Decide whether Direction256Toward should stop landing one step short
items.details: `Direction256Toward()` (was `Desired_Facing256()`) returns `DirType::kEast - 1` for a target due east, `kSouth - 1` due south, `kSouthEast - 1` on the exact south-east diagonal and `kNorthWest - 1` on the exact north-west one; north, west, north-east and south-west are exact. The cause is the `- 1` in `fraction = 0x40 - fraction - 1` in `src/game/sim/direction.cc`, which is right for every non-exact angle (it makes that half of the quadrant round the same way as the other) and wrong only when `smaller * 32 / bigger` divides exactly. `direction_test.cc` pins the current results (`EastAndSouthLandOneStepShort`, `TwoDiagonalsLandOneStepShort`), and `src/ra/core/coord_test.cc` notes it too.
items.author: agent

The pinning tests in `direction_test.cc` and `ra/core/coord_test.cc` expect the exact values, and the hashes of four UI scripts whose in-mission screenshots shifted were re-recorded.

items.details: The first `tools/coverage.py --tests game_sim src/game/sim/direction.h src/game/sim/direction.cc` of this run failed while linking: `gtest_discover_tests` ran `build-coverage/src/engine/window/engine_window_test` and got `Result: Bus error`, which stopped the build. items.title: Fix the row stride and missing lock in Red Alert's Write_PCX_File
items.details:
`ra::Write_PCX_File()` steps through `pic.view().pixels()` by `pic.width() + pic.view().x_add()`, which leaves out the buffer's `pitch()`, and never locks the view: for a surface-backed `PixelBuffer` the rows are skewed, and while the surface is unlocked `pixels()` is empty and the first `subspan` runs past its end. Every caller passes a memory buffer, so it is latent.

The engine's writer had the same defect, fixed in `f588fbad` (lock the view, use `stride()`); `engine/gfx/pcx_file_test.cc`'s `WritesASurfaceSkippingItsRowPadding` is the test to copy. Goes away by itself if RA switches to the engine's writer.

items.title: Decide whether a PCX scanline is padded to an even length
items.details: `WritePcxFile()` sets the header's `bytes_per_line` to the picture's width. The PCX specification requires an even number, so a picture of odd width is written with an odd one. The games' own reader accepts any value not below the width; a strict third-party reader may not. Padding means writing one extra byte per row for odd widths, which changes the file bytes (and any recorded screenshot hash of an odd-width picture).
